title: My friend’s house
intro: To show that something belongs to someone, English adds ’s to the owner: my brother’s car. For things (not people), we usually use “of”: the end of the film. Leaving out the ’s (“my friend house”) is a very common mistake.

rules.rule: Plural owner ending in -s: add only ’.
For things and places, “of” is more natural.

mistakes.wrong: I went to my friend house.
mistakes.right: I went to my friend’s house.
mistakes.why: Add ’s to show it belongs to your friend.

mistakes.right: The leg of the table is broken.

ex.y: cousin’s place = the place of my cousin

ex.q: Write your name at the top ___.
ex.y: For things: the top of the page.

ex.q: We are going to my uncle wedding.
ex.fixed: We are going to my uncle’s wedding.

ex.q: This is Priya___ laptop, not mine.

ex.a: My sister’s husband works in a bank.

ex.q: Say it with ’s: “the car of my father”.

talk: Describe your best friend’s home or your family members’ jobs. Use ’s at least four times: my mother’s…, my friend’s….
